key_insight: Machine learning can diagnose degradation mechanisms in simulated lead-free solar cells, but strong predictions require representative training data.
engineering_relevance: Replacing Spiro-OMeTAD with CuI raises simulated efficiency from 19.6% to 21.6%, almost entirely through improved fill factor.
method: Generate approximately 42,000 SCAPS-1D simulations of RbSn₀.₅Ge₀.₅I₃ solar cells.
Compare surrogate models trained on factorial-grid and Latin hypercube samples.
Identify six degradation mechanisms using multi-label classification of temperature- and illumination-dependent open-circuit voltage.
evidence_signal: The classifier achieves macro F1 = 0.938 versus 0.687 for a physics-rule baseline; XGBoost R² falls from 0.9997 on held-out grid points to 0.58 on independently sampled devices, while Latin hypercube training restores R² = 0.995.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based, and the classifier does not generalize to degradation-mechanism combinations absent from training.
paper_title: Interpretable machine learning diagnosis of degradation mechanisms in lead-free $RbSn_{0.5}Ge_{0.5}I_{3}$ solar cells from temperature- and illumination-dependent electrical measurements
